origins.name: Origins
origins.blurb: The first digital images, and a new question: can a machine see?

classical.name: Classical vision
classical.blurb: Geometry, physics and mathematics, designed by hand one step at a time.

features.name: Features & machine learning
features.blurb: Hand-crafted features plus statistical classifiers take vision out of the lab.

deep.name: Big data & deep learning
deep.blurb: ImageNet and GPUs make deep neural networks the default method.

transformer.name: Transformers & multimodality
transformer.blurb: Attention replaces convolution; images and language share one space.

generative.name: Generation & foundation models
generative.blurb: Image, video and 3D generation, and foundation models shared across tasks.

firstDigitalImage.title: The first digital image
firstDigitalImage.summary: Russell Kirsch used the SEAC computer at the US National Bureau of Standards to scan a photo of his son into a 176×176 pixel grid.
firstDigitalImage.impact: The first image stored as numbers in a computer.

perceptron.title: Rosenblatt's perceptron
perceptron.summary: Frank Rosenblatt described the perceptron, a single-layer neural network that learned to classify simple visual patterns from data.
perceptron.impact: Machines that learn from examples: the root of deep learning.

visualCortex.title: Simple and complex cells in the visual cortex
visualCortex.summary: Hubel and Wiesel recorded cells in the cat visual cortex that fire only for edges at a specific orientation, organised in layers.
visualCortex.impact: Layered receptive fields directly inspired CNNs.

kalmanFilter.title: The Kalman filter
kalmanFilter.summary: Rudolf Kálmán showed how to estimate a hidden state from noisy measurements: predict, then correct with each new observation.
kalmanFilter.impact: The backbone of tracking, from radar to object trackers in video.

houghTransform.title: The Hough transform
houghTransform.summary: Paul Hough patented a way to find straight lines in bubble-chamber photos by letting each pixel vote in a parameter space.
houghTransform.impact: Still the standard way to find lines, circles and lanes.

blocksWorld.title: Blocks world
blocksWorld.summary: Larry Roberts' MIT thesis recovered three-dimensional shape from a single two-dimensional photo of polyhedral blocks.
blocksWorld.impact: The first 3D vision problem: geometry from a flat image.

fastFourierTransform.title: The fast Fourier transform (FFT)
fastFourierTransform.summary: Cooley and Tukey published the FFT, cutting the cost of frequency analysis of signals and images from quadratic to near-linear.
fastFourierTransform.impact: Made frequency filtering, compression and fast convolution practical.

summerVisionProject.title: The MIT Summer Vision Project
summerVisionProject.summary: Seymour Papert set a group of students the goal of solving segmentation and object recognition over a single summer.
summerVisionProject.impact: A classic lesson: vision is far harder than it looks.

kMeans.title: k-means clustering
kMeans.summary: James MacQueen named and analysed k-means: assign each point to its nearest centre, then move each centre to the mean of its cluster.
kMeans.impact: The simplest clustering, later used for colour quantisation and visual-word codebooks.

perceptronsBook.title: Perceptrons, the book
perceptronsBook.summary: Minsky and Papert proved that single-layer perceptrons cannot learn functions such as XOR or whether a figure is connected.
perceptronsBook.impact: Cooled neural-network research for nearly two decades, until backpropagation.

ccdSensor.title: The CCD image sensor
ccdSensor.summary: Willard Boyle and George Smith at Bell Labs invented the charge-coupled device, turning light into charge read out pixel by pixel; Nobel Prize in Physics 2009.
ccdSensor.impact: Made digital cameras possible, the source of images for all later vision.

shapeFromShading.title: Shape from shading
shapeFromShading.summary: Berthold Horn's MIT thesis recovered the three-dimensional shape of a surface from the shading in a single image.
shapeFromShading.impact: Started "shape from X" and depth estimation.

dudaHartLines.title: Hough transform for lines and curves
dudaHartLines.summary: Duda and Hart reparametrised the Hough transform with (ρ, θ), avoiding infinite slopes and extending it to circles.
dudaHartLines.impact: The form of the Hough transform every library, OpenCV included, still uses.

pictorialStructures.title: Pictorial structures
pictorialStructures.summary: Fischler and Elschlager described an object as parts joined by springs, then searched for the placement that best fits the image.
pictorialStructures.impact: The root of part-based models; deformable part models and pose estimation build on it.

cooperativeStereo.title: Cooperative stereo
cooperativeStereo.summary: Marr and Poggio proposed a cooperative algorithm that matches points between left and right images to recover depth, using uniqueness and continuity constraints.
cooperativeStereo.impact: Made stereo matching a research field of its own.

otsuThreshold.title: Otsu thresholding
otsuThreshold.summary: Nobuyuki Otsu chose the foreground/background threshold automatically by maximising the between-class variance of the histogram.
otsuThreshold.impact: The default binarisation for OCR and inspection.

structureFromMotion.title: Ullman's structure from motion
structureFromMotion.summary: Shimon Ullman proved that three views of four non-coplanar points are enough to recover 3D structure and motion.
structureFromMotion.impact: The theoretical root of structure from motion and SLAM.

neocognitron.title: Neocognitron
neocognitron.summary: Kunihiko Fukushima built a layered network of S-cells and C-cells modelled on the visual cortex, recognising handwriting regardless of position.
neocognitron.impact: The first convolution-plus-pooling design, ancestor of the CNN.

marrHildreth.title: Marr–Hildreth edge detection
marrHildreth.summary: Marr and Hildreth located edges at zero crossings of the Laplacian of a Gaussian-smoothed image, at several scales.
marrHildreth.impact: Biology-inspired edges and the seed of multi-scale analysis.

photometricStereo.title: Photometric stereo
photometricStereo.summary: Robert Woodham photographed an object from one viewpoint under several light directions and solved for the surface normal at every pixel.
photometricStereo.impact: Still a standard for detailed surface capture in inspection and heritage scanning.

opticalFlow.title: Optical flow
opticalFlow.summary: Horn and Schunck, alongside Lucas and Kanade, showed how to estimate per-pixel motion between two frames.
opticalFlow.impact: The basis of tracking, stabilisation and video analysis.

ransac.title: RANSAC
ransac.summary: Fischler and Bolles fitted models by sampling a few points at random, counting how many agree, and keeping the model with the most support.
ransac.impact: The standard outlier-robust fit for stitching and 3D.

generalizedHough.title: The generalised Hough transform
generalizedHough.summary: Dana Ballard extended the Hough transform to arbitrary shapes using a lookup table of edge-to-centre vectors.
generalizedHough.impact: One of the first shape-based detectors.

essentialMatrix.title: The essential matrix and the eight-point algorithm
essentialMatrix.summary: Longuet-Higgins showed that eight point correspondences between two images determine the relative camera motion and scene structure.
essentialMatrix.impact: The maths of two-view geometry, SfM and SLAM.

lucasKanade.title: Lucas–Kanade
lucasKanade.summary: Lucas and Kanade estimated how a small patch moves with an iterative gradient-based method, assuming constant motion inside the patch.
lucasKanade.impact: For decades the most used optical-flow and feature-tracking (KLT) method.

marrVision.title: David Marr's three levels of analysis
marrVision.summary: The book Vision proposed splitting the problem into computational, representation-and-algorithm, and implementation levels.
marrVision.impact: Turned vision into a structured science.

laplacianPyramid.title: The Laplacian pyramid
laplacianPyramid.summary: Burt and Adelson split an image into frequency bands at several resolutions, each keeping only the detail the coarser level lacks.
laplacianPyramid.impact: A multi-scale workhorse for blending, compression and, later, feature pyramids.

scaleSpace.title: Scale-space theory
scaleSpace.summary: Witkin and Koenderink formalised looking at an image across a continuous range of Gaussian blurs, the scale space.
scaleSpace.impact: The theory behind SIFT and feature pyramids.

markovRandomFields.title: Markov random fields for images
markovRandomFields.summary: Stuart and Donald Geman modelled images as Markov random fields where each pixel depends on its neighbours, restoring noisy images with Gibbs sampling.
markovRandomFields.impact: The probabilistic framework for denoising, segmentation and stereo for two decades.

backpropagation.title: Backpropagation
backpropagation.summary: Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams popularised backpropagation for training multi-layer neural networks.
backpropagation.impact: How almost every vision model still learns.

cannyEdges.title: The Canny edge detector
cannyEdges.summary: John Canny framed edge detection as an optimisation with three criteria: few errors, accurate localisation, and one response per edge.
cannyEdges.impact: A classic shipped in every vision library.

tsaiCalibration.title: Tsai camera calibration
tsaiCalibration.summary: Roger Tsai gave an accurate calibration procedure, including lens distortion, for off-the-shelf cameras and lenses.

marchingCubes.title: Marching cubes
marchingCubes.summary: Lorensen and Cline turned volume data such as CT scans into triangle meshes by checking how the surface crosses each small cube.
marchingCubes.impact: The standard way to extract meshes from volumes, used even by KinectFusion and NeRF.

activeContours.title: Active contours (snakes)
activeContours.summary: Kass, Witkin and Terzopoulos modelled an object boundary as an elastic curve that deforms to lock onto image edges.

harrisCorner.title: The Harris corner detector
harrisCorner.summary: Harris and Stephens detected corners from the local gradient matrix, points that are easy to find again across images.
harrisCorner.impact: The standard keypoint for tracking and matching.

convNetBackprop.title: Convolutional networks trained with backpropagation
convNetBackprop.summary: Yann LeCun and colleagues trained a convolutional network with backpropagation to read handwritten zip codes.
convNetBackprop.impact: The modern CNN recipe, first assembled.

peronaMalik.title: Anisotropic diffusion
peronaMalik.summary: Perona and Malik blurred images like heat diffusion but slowed it at edges, removing noise while keeping boundaries sharp.
peronaMalik.impact: Started the family of edge-preserving filters such as bilateral filtering.

eigenfaces.title: Eigenfaces
eigenfaces.summary: Turk and Pentland used principal component analysis to represent a face with a few dozen coefficients.

jpeg.title: The JPEG standard
jpeg.summary: JPEG applied the discrete cosine transform to 8×8 blocks plus quantisation to compress photos by a factor of ten or more.
jpeg.impact: Made photos shareable and built the web's image data.

icp.title: Iterative Closest Point (ICP)
icp.summary: Besl and McKay aligned two point clouds by iterating: pair each point with its nearest neighbour, then solve for the best rotation and translation.
icp.impact: The basic 3D registration algorithm for scanning, robotics and self-driving.

goodFeatures.title: Good Features to Track
goodFeatures.summary: Shi and Tomasi chose points to track by the smaller eigenvalue of the gradient matrix, exactly what Lucas–Kanade needs.
goodFeatures.impact: OpenCV's goodFeaturesToTrack, behind the KLT tracker and visual odometry.

supportVectorMachines.title: Support vector machines
supportVectorMachines.summary: Cortes and Vapnik published the soft-margin SVM: a classifier that finds the hyperplane with the widest margin between classes.
supportVectorMachines.impact: The default classifier for hand-crafted features until 2012.

facade.title: Façade: architecture from photographs
facade.summary: Debevec, Taylor and Malik combined simple block models with a few photos to reconstruct and render buildings realistically.
facade.impact: Launched image-based modelling and rendering, a precursor of modern photogrammetry.

fisherfaces.title: Fisherfaces
fisherfaces.summary: Belhumeur, Hespanha and Kriegman used linear discriminant analysis instead of PCA, keeping directions that separate people and ignoring lighting changes.
fisherfaces.impact: Face recognition far more robust to lighting than eigenfaces.

bilateralFilter.title: The bilateral filter
bilateralFilter.summary: Tomasi and Manduchi smoothed images with weights based on both spatial distance and colour difference, preserving sharp edges.
bilateralFilter.impact: The edge-preserving denoiser in every photo pipeline.

condensation.title: CONDENSATION tracking
condensation.summary: Isard and Blake used a particle filter to track object contours through cluttered video.

lenet5.title: LeNet-5 and MNIST
lenet5.summary: Yann LeCun and colleagues trained a convolutional network to read handwritten digits, deployed commercially to process bank cheques.
lenet5.impact: CNNs in production a decade before the deep learning boom.

sift.title: SIFT
sift.summary: David Lowe introduced local features invariant to scale and rotation, letting the same object be matched across different images.
sift.impact: The backbone of stitching, SLAM and retrieval in the 2000s.

textureSynthesis.title: Efros–Leung texture synthesis
textureSynthesis.summary: Efros and Leung grew new texture from a sample by filling in one pixel at a time from similar neighbourhoods in the source.
textureSynthesis.impact: Early non-parametric generation, precursor of inpainting.

backgroundSubtraction.title: Background subtraction with mixtures of Gaussians
backgroundSubtraction.summary: Stauffer and Grimson modelled each background pixel as an adaptive mixture of Gaussians, separating moving objects even as the scene slowly changes.
backgroundSubtraction.impact: The core of surveillance cameras and traffic counters for years.

morphableModel.title: 3D morphable face model
morphableModel.summary: Blanz and Vetter learned a linear space of 3D face shape and texture from scans and fitted it to a single photo.
morphableModel.impact: The basis of 3D face reconstruction, animation and avatars.

normalizedCuts.title: Normalized cuts
normalizedCuts.summary: Shi and Malik cast segmentation as cutting a graph of pixels, solved with eigenvectors.

zhangCalibration.title: Zhang's camera calibration
zhangCalibration.summary: Zhengyou Zhang calibrated a camera from a few photos of a flat checkerboard at different angles.
zhangCalibration.impact: The calibration method built into OpenCV.

multipleViewGeometry.title: Multiple View Geometry (the book)
multipleViewGeometry.summary: Hartley and Zisserman gathered projective geometry, the fundamental matrix, triangulation and bundle adjustment in one book.

violaJones.title: Viola–Jones real-time face detection
violaJones.summary: A detector built from Haar features, AdaBoost and a cascade of classifiers, running in real time on the consumer CPUs of the day.
violaJones.impact: Put face detection into cameras and phones.

graphCuts.title: Energy minimisation with graph cuts
graphCuts.summary: Boykov, Veksler and Zabih solved pixel-labelling problems (segmentation, stereo) quickly with max-flow algorithms.
graphCuts.impact: The engine behind interactive cut-out tools like GrabCut.

localBinaryPatterns.title: Local binary patterns (LBP)
localBinaryPatterns.summary: Ojala and colleagues described texture by comparing each pixel with its neighbours, producing a brightness-invariant binary code.
localBinaryPatterns.impact: A light, fast feature for faces and surface inspection.

meanShift.title: Mean shift
meanShift.summary: Comaniciu and Meer used mean shift to find density peaks in colour-position space for segmentation and smoothing.
meanShift.impact: Clustering without a preset k, for segmentation and tracking.

middleburyStereo.title: The Middlebury stereo benchmark
middleburyStereo.summary: Scharstein and Szeliski classified stereo algorithms and released images with ground truth plus an online ranking.
middleburyStereo.impact: A template for leaderboard benchmarks; stereo improved fast through fair comparison.

bagOfVisualWords.title: Bag of visual words (Video Google)
bagOfVisualWords.summary: Sivic and Zisserman quantised local features into "visual words" and searched images the way search engines search text.
bagOfVisualWords.impact: The dominant image representation for a decade.

poissonEditing.title: Poisson image editing
poissonEditing.summary: Pérez, Gangnet and Blake blended a region seamlessly into another image by solving a Poisson equation on gradients.
poissonEditing.impact: The basis of seamless cloning and object removal.

ssim.title: SSIM
ssim.summary: Wang and colleagues measured image quality by structural, luminance and contrast similarity instead of per-pixel error.
ssim.impact: The standard metric for compression and restoration.

grabCut.title: GrabCut
grabCut.summary: Rother, Kolmogorov and Blake needed only a box around the object; iterated graph cuts with colour models separated it from the background.
grabCut.impact: Interactive cut-out found in Office, OpenCV and many photo editors.

caltech101.title: Caltech 101
caltech101.summary: Fei-Fei, Fergus and Perona released a 101-category dataset to test learning recognition from very few examples.
caltech101.impact: The popular multi-class benchmark before PASCAL VOC and ImageNet.

graphSegmentation.title: Efficient graph-based segmentation
graphSegmentation.summary: Felzenszwalb and Huttenlocher merged pixels into regions on a graph, stopping when the difference between regions exceeds that within them, in near-linear time.
graphSegmentation.impact: Fast superpixels, the seed of Selective Search and R-CNN.

hog.title: HOG features
hog.summary: Dalal and Triggs described objects with histograms of oriented gradients and paired them with an SVM to detect pedestrians.

pascalVoc.title: PASCAL VOC
pascalVoc.summary: An annual challenge with a shared dataset and evaluation protocol for classification, detection and segmentation.
pascalVoc.impact: Set the culture of public benchmarks.

nonLocalMeans.title: Non-local means
nonLocalMeans.summary: Buades, Coll and Morel denoised each pixel by averaging patches that look like it anywhere in the image, not only nearby.
nonLocalMeans.impact: Opened the era of patch-based denoising such as BM3D.

deepAutoencoders.title: Layer-wise pre-trained deep networks
deepAutoencoders.summary: Hinton and Salakhutdinov trained deep networks by pre-training one layer at a time, compressing images far better than PCA.
deepAutoencoders.impact: Showed deep nets could be trained.

surf.title: SURF
surf.summary: Bay, Tuytelaars and Van Gool sped up scale-invariant features with integral images and box filters.
surf.impact: Real-time feature matching for robotics and AR.

photoTourism.title: Photo Tourism and large-scale SfM
photoTourism.summary: Snavely, Seitz and Szeliski reconstructed 3D scenes and camera positions from thousands of tourist photos on the Internet.
photoTourism.impact: 3D from Internet photos, forerunner of COLMAP.

spatialPyramid.title: Spatial pyramid matching
spatialPyramid.summary: Lazebnik, Schmid and Ponce counted visual words over finer and finer grids, adding layout to the bag of words.
spatialPyramid.impact: The strongest image-classification pipeline before deep learning.

seamCarving.title: Seam carving
seamCarving.summary: Avidan and Shamir resized images by repeatedly removing the lowest-energy seam, leaving important objects untouched.

ptam.title: PTAM
ptam.summary: Klein and Murray split camera tracking and 3D mapping into two parallel threads, running in real time on a laptop for AR.
ptam.impact: The architecture later visual SLAM systems such as ORB-SLAM follow.

deformablePartModels.title: Deformable part models (DPM)
deformablePartModels.summary: Felzenszwalb and colleagues modelled objects as a root template plus parts that can shift, learned on HOG features.

imagenet.title: ImageNet
imagenet.summary: Fei-Fei Li's group built a dataset of over 14 million images labelled along WordNet; the ILSVRC challenge started in 2010.
imagenet.impact: The scale of data deep learning needed.

patchMatch.title: PatchMatch
patchMatch.summary: Barnes and colleagues found matching patches between images very fast with random guesses propagated to neighbours.
patchMatch.impact: Photoshop's content-aware fill; the propagation idea returned in stereo.

kinectPose.title: Human pose estimation on Kinect
kinectPose.summary: Shotton and colleagues used random forests on depth images to recognise body parts in real time.
kinectPose.impact: Pose estimation in millions of homes; the power of synthetic data.

kinectFusion.title: KinectFusion
kinectFusion.summary: Newcombe and colleagues used a Kinect depth camera, GPU ICP and a TSDF volume to build a 3D model of a room in real time.
kinectFusion.impact: Brought real-time dense 3D reconstruction to everyone.

orb.title: ORB features
orb.summary: Rublee and colleagues combined FAST keypoints with rotation-aware binary BRIEF descriptors, far faster than SIFT and patent-free.
orb.impact: The default feature for SLAM and mobile apps.

kittiBenchmark.title: The KITTI benchmark
kittiBenchmark.summary: Geiger, Lenz and Urtasun recorded a real car with stereo cameras, LiDAR and GPS, with benchmarks for stereo, optical flow, odometry and 3D detection.

alexnet.title: AlexNet
alexnet.summary: Krizhevsky, Sutskever and Hinton trained a convolutional network on GPUs, cutting the ILSVRC 2012 top-5 error from around 26% to 15.3%.
alexnet.impact: The moment the field switched to deep learning.

dropout.title: Dropout
dropout.summary: Hinton and colleagues randomly switched off half the neurons at each training step, so the network cannot rely on any single feature.
dropout.impact: The key regularisation that kept AlexNet and other large networks from overfitting.

visualizingConvnets.title: Visualising convolutional networks (ZFNet)
visualizingConvnets.summary: Zeiler and Fergus used deconvolutional networks to show what each CNN layer learns, from edges and textures to object parts.
visualizingConvnets.impact: Opened the CNN black box; won ILSVRC 2013.

variationalAutoencoder.title: Variational autoencoders (VAE)
variationalAutoencoder.summary: Kingma and Welling combined neural networks with variational inference to learn a continuous latent space that can be sampled.
variationalAutoencoder.impact: Its latent space later powered Stable Diffusion.

selectiveSearch.title: Selective Search
selectiveSearch.summary: Uijlings and colleagues merged superpixels by colour, texture and size to produce about two thousand regions likely to hold objects.
selectiveSearch.impact: The region proposals behind R-CNN and Fast R-CNN.

rcnn.title: R-CNN
rcnn.summary: Girshick and colleagues combined region proposals with CNN features, sharply improving detection accuracy.

gan.title: Generative adversarial networks
gan.summary: Goodfellow and colleagues pitted a generator against a discriminator, producing new images that grew steadily more realistic.

microsoftCoco.title: The MS COCO dataset
microsoftCoco.summary: Microsoft COCO offered over 300,000 everyday-scene images with boxes, per-instance masks and sentence captions.
microsoftCoco.impact: Still the standard detection and segmentation benchmark.

deepFace.title: DeepFace
deepFace.summary: Facebook combined 3D face alignment with a deep network, reaching near-human accuracy on LFW.
deepFace.impact: Deep face recognition at product scale.

vggNet.title: VGGNet
vggNet.summary: Simonyan and Zisserman stacked nothing but 3×3 convolutions very deep and placed at the top of ILSVRC 2014.
vggNet.impact: A simple backbone used for years.

googLeNet.title: GoogLeNet and the Inception block
googLeNet.summary: Szegedy and colleagues ran convolutions of several sizes in parallel inside Inception blocks and won ILSVRC 2014 with far fewer parameters.
googLeNet.impact: Architectures tuned for accuracy and compute.

superResolutionCnn.title: SRCNN: super-resolution with a CNN
superResolutionCnn.summary: Dong and colleagues used a small convolutional network to upscale images, beating traditional super-resolution methods.

fullyConvolutionalNetworks.title: Fully convolutional networks (FCN)
fullyConvolutionalNetworks.summary: Long, Shelhamer and Darrell replaced fully connected layers with convolutions to predict a label for every pixel.

deepLab.title: DeepLab and atrous convolution
deepLab.summary: Chen and colleagues used dilated (atrous) convolution to widen the receptive field without losing resolution, plus a CRF to sharpen boundaries.

deepPose.title: DeepPose
deepPose.summary: Toshev and Szegedy (Google) had a CNN regress body-joint coordinates directly, then refined them with a cascade of CNNs.
deepPose.impact: The first deep-learning pose estimator, paving the way for OpenPose.

twoStream.title: Two-stream networks for action recognition
twoStream.summary: Simonyan and Zisserman used one CNN on RGB frames and one on optical flow, fusing them to recognise actions.
twoStream.impact: The standard video-recognition design until large 3D CNNs.

batchNormalization.title: Batch normalisation
batchNormalization.summary: Ioffe and Szegedy normalised each layer's outputs over a mini-batch, making training much faster and more stable.

faceNet.title: FaceNet
faceNet.summary: Google learned a face embedding with a triplet loss, where distance reflects how alike two people are.
faceNet.impact: Embeddings became standard for face recognition.

fastRcnn.title: Fast R-CNN
fastRcnn.summary: Ross Girshick computed features once per image and pooled them per region with RoI pooling, making inference hundreds of times faster than R-CNN.
fastRcnn.impact: Two-stage detection, trained end to end.

flowNet.title: FlowNet
flowNet.summary: Dosovitskiy and colleagues estimated optical flow directly with a CNN trained on the synthetic Flying Chairs data.
flowNet.impact: Moved optical flow to deep learning.

unet.title: U-Net
unet.summary: An encoder–decoder architecture with skip connections that segments biomedical images accurately from very little training data.
unet.impact: Backbone of medical segmentation and diffusion.

fasterRcnn.title: Faster R-CNN
fasterRcnn.summary: Ren and colleagues added a region proposal network with anchors, so the network proposes its own candidate regions.

yolo.title: YOLO
yolo.summary: Redmon and colleagues treated detection as a single regression over the whole image, reaching real-time speed.

neuralStyleTransfer.title: Neural style transfer
neuralStyleTransfer.summary: Gatys, Ecker and Bethge separated content and style using CNN features and repainted photos in the style of a painting.
neuralStyleTransfer.impact: The public's first look at AI-made images.

dcgan.title: DCGAN
dcgan.summary: Radford and colleagues set out convolutional design rules that made GANs train stably and produce sharp images.

ssdDetector.title: SSD
ssdDetector.summary: Liu and colleagues detected objects in a single stage on feature maps at several scales.
ssdDetector.impact: With YOLO, shaped mobile one-stage detectors.

resnet.title: ResNet
resnet.summary: He and colleagues added residual skip connections, trained networks over 100 layers deep, and won ILSVRC 2015.

orbSlam.title: ORB-SLAM
orbSlam.summary: Mur-Artal, Montiel and Tardós built a complete SLAM system on ORB features with tracking, mapping and loop closing, in real time from one camera.
orbSlam.impact: The most used open-source visual SLAM in robotics and AR.

c3d.title: C3D
c3d.summary: Tran and colleagues (Facebook) trained 3D convolutions on large video clip sets, giving generic features for appearance and motion.
c3d.impact: Showed 3D CNNs learn video features, leading to I3D.

denseNet.title: DenseNet
denseNet.summary: Huang and colleagues connected each layer to every later layer in a block, reusing features with few parameters.
denseNet.impact: Popular in medical imaging for its efficiency.

sortTracking.title: SORT: multi-object tracking
sortTracking.summary: Bewley and colleagues linked detector outputs across frames with a Kalman filter and the Hungarian algorithm, extremely simple and fast.

cityscapes.title: The Cityscapes dataset
cityscapes.summary: Cordts and colleagues annotated street scenes from 50 cities with fine per-pixel labels.

openPose.title: OpenPose
openPose.summary: Cao and colleagues estimated the skeletons of many people at once using part affinity fields, in real time.

pix2pix.title: pix2pix
pix2pix.summary: Isola and colleagues used a conditional GAN for image-to-image translation: sketches to photos, maps to aerial views, day to night.
pix2pix.impact: One framework for paired image-to-image tasks.

featurePyramidNetworks.title: Feature pyramid networks (FPN)
featurePyramidNetworks.summary: Lin and colleagues merged deep and shallow features along a top-down path, detecting both small and large objects well.
featurePyramidNetworks.impact: A standard part of modern detectors.

stackedHourglass.title: Stacked hourglass networks
stackedHourglass.summary: Newell, Yang and Deng stacked downsample-then-upsample (hourglass) blocks to predict joint heatmaps, refining them stage by stage.
stackedHourglass.impact: The leading pose backbone before HRNet.

colmap.title: COLMAP: structure-from-motion revisited
colmap.summary: Schönberger and Frahm reworked incremental SfM for accuracy and robustness, released as COLMAP.
colmap.impact: The default SfM tool, providing camera poses for almost every NeRF and splatting paper.

maskRcnn.title: Mask R-CNN
maskRcnn.summary: Extended Faster R-CNN with a mask prediction branch, producing per-instance segmentation.

cycleGan.title: CycleGAN
cycleGan.summary: Zhu and colleagues translated images between two domains without paired data, using a cycle-consistency constraint.

mobileNets.title: MobileNets
mobileNets.summary: Howard and colleagues used depthwise separable convolutions to build small, fast networks for phones and embedded devices.
mobileNets.impact: Put CNNs on phones and IoT.

kineticsI3d.title: Kinetics and I3D
kineticsI3d.summary: Carreira and Zisserman introduced the Kinetics action dataset and "inflated" 2D CNNs into 3D for action recognition in video.

transformerArchitecture.title: The Transformer architecture
transformerArchitecture.summary: The paper Attention Is All You Need dropped recurrence and convolution entirely in favour of self-attention.
transformerArchitecture.impact: Three years later it displaced CNNs in vision.

focalLoss.title: RetinaNet and focal loss
focalLoss.summary: Lin and colleagues down-weighted easy background examples, letting a single-stage detector beat two-stage accuracy for the first time.
focalLoss.impact: The default loss for class imbalance.

pointNet.title: PointNet
pointNet.summary: Qi and colleagues (Stanford) processed raw point clouds with a shared per-point MLP followed by max-pooling, so point order does not matter.
pointNet.impact: Deep learning on raw 3D data, the basis of LiDAR detection.

gradCam.title: Grad-CAM
gradCam.summary: Selvaraju and colleagues used the gradient of the predicted class on the last feature map to draw a heatmap of where the model looked.
gradCam.impact: The most common way to explain CNNs and catch models that learned shortcuts.

seNet.title: Squeeze-and-Excitation networks
seNet.summary: Hu, Shen and Sun squeezed each channel to one number and learned weights to boost useful channels and damp others; winner of ImageNet 2017.
seNet.impact: Channel attention, a block added to most modern backbones.

panopticSegmentation.title: Panoptic segmentation
panopticSegmentation.summary: Kirillov and colleagues unified semantic ("stuff") and instance ("things") segmentation into one task and one metric, PQ.
panopticSegmentation.impact: Every pixel gets a class and an instance.

arcFace.title: ArcFace
arcFace.summary: Deng and colleagues added an angular margin to the softmax loss, producing more discriminative face features.

yoloV3.title: YOLOv3
yoloV3.summary: Redmon and Farhadi added multi-scale predictions and a Darknet-53 backbone, balancing speed and accuracy well.

styleGan.title: StyleGAN
styleGan.summary: Karras and colleagues at NVIDIA controlled each level of detail through style vectors, generating faces almost indistinguishable from real ones.
styleGan.impact: Peak GAN quality; the start of deepfake worries.

bigGan.title: BigGAN
bigGan.summary: Brock, Donahue and Simonyan (DeepMind) scaled GANs to very large batches and models, generating class-conditional ImageNet images of unprecedented quality.
bigGan.impact: Showed that scale is key for generative models.

fcosAnchorFree.title: FCOS: anchor-free detection
fcosAnchorFree.summary: Tian and colleagues predicted each location's distance to the four box sides, dropping anchors entirely.
fcosAnchorFree.impact: Anchor-free design adopted by later YOLOs.

efficientNet.title: EfficientNet
efficientNet.summary: Tan and Le scaled depth, width and resolution together with one compound coefficient, on a base network found by architecture search.
efficientNet.impact: High accuracy for far less compute.

momentumContrast.title: MoCo: contrastive self-supervised learning
momentumContrast.summary: He and colleagues learned image representations without labels by telling augmentations of one image apart from a queue of others.

slowFast.title: SlowFast networks
slowFast.summary: Feichtenhofer and colleagues (Facebook) paired a slow pathway reading few frames for context with a light fast pathway capturing motion.
slowFast.impact: A leading video-recognition design, inspired by biological vision.

hrNet.title: HRNet
hrNet.summary: Sun and colleagues (Microsoft) kept a high-resolution branch through the whole network, exchanging information with lower-resolution ones throughout.
hrNet.impact: The standard backbone for pose estimation and dense prediction.

simClr.title: SimCLR
simClr.summary: Chen and colleagues showed that strong augmentation, large batches and a projection head bring contrastive learning close to supervised results.
simClr.impact: A simple recipe that spread self-supervision.

raftFlow.title: RAFT
raftFlow.summary: Teed and Deng estimated optical flow by repeatedly looking up a full all-pairs correlation volume; ECCV 2020 best paper.

nerf.title: NeRF
nerf.summary: Represented a three-dimensional scene as a neural network, synthesising new viewpoints from only a few dozen photos.
nerf.impact: A scene as a learnable function, not a mesh.

detr.title: DETR
detr.summary: Carion and colleagues detected objects with a transformer, removing anchors and the NMS post-processing step.

denoisingDiffusion.title: Denoising diffusion models (DDPM)
denoisingDiffusion.summary: Ho, Jain and Abbeel generated images by learning to reverse a step-by-step noising process, matching GAN quality.
denoisingDiffusion.impact: The basis of today's image and video generators.

visionTransformer.title: Vision Transformer (ViT)
visionTransformer.summary: An image is cut into 16×16 patches and fed to a transformer as a sequence of tokens, beating CNNs given enough data.
visionTransformer.impact: Vision and language share one architecture.

dataEfficientTransformers.title: DeiT
dataEfficientTransformers.summary: Touvron and colleagues trained ViTs on ImageNet-1k alone using distillation and strong augmentation.

byol.title: BYOL
byol.summary: Grill and colleagues (DeepMind) learned representations by having a network predict the output of a slowly averaged copy of itself, with no negative pairs.
byol.impact: Showed self-supervised learning needs no negatives, leading to DINO.

dallE.title: DALL·E
dallE.summary: OpenAI generated images from text descriptions with an autoregressive transformer over text and image tokens.

clip.title: CLIP
clip.summary: Trained on 400 million image–text pairs from the web, classifying unseen classes without labels (zero-shot).
clip.impact: The basis of language-driven search and generation.

swinTransformer.title: Swin Transformer
swinTransformer.summary: Liu and colleagues computed attention in shifted windows and built hierarchical features like a CNN.
swinTransformer.impact: A general transformer backbone; ICCV 2021 best paper.

dino.title: DINO
dino.summary: Caron and colleagues trained ViTs without labels through self-distillation between teacher and student networks.
dino.impact: Attention maps that segment objects on their own.

segFormer.title: SegFormer
segFormer.summary: Xie and colleagues paired a hierarchical transformer encoder with a light MLP decoder for semantic segmentation.
segFormer.impact: Transformer segmentation light enough to deploy.

maskedAutoencoders.title: Masked autoencoders (MAE)
maskedAutoencoders.summary: He and colleagues masked 75% of image patches at random and trained a ViT to reconstruct them.

vqgan.title: VQGAN: taming transformers
vqgan.summary: Esser, Rombach and Ommer compressed images into discrete token grids with a GAN loss, then let a Transformer generate tokens for high-resolution images.
vqgan.impact: The image tokeniser and latent space Stable Diffusion builds on.

byteTrack.title: ByteTrack
byteTrack.summary: Zhang and colleagues also matched low-score boxes to tracks instead of discarding them, losing far fewer occluded objects.
byteTrack.impact: A simple, strong tracker, the default in many YOLO pipelines.

mask2Former.title: Mask2Former
mask2Former.summary: Cheng and colleagues (Meta) used mask queries with masked attention to solve semantic, instance and panoptic segmentation with one architecture.
mask2Former.impact: One architecture for every kind of segmentation.

convNext.title: ConvNeXt
convNext.summary: Liu and colleagues modernised ResNet step by step with transformer design choices and matched Swin's accuracy.

latentDiffusion.title: Latent diffusion and Stable Diffusion
latentDiffusion.summary: Rombach and colleagues ran diffusion in a latent space, cutting compute cost sharply; the model was released publicly in 2022.

dallE2.title: DALL·E 2
dallE2.summary: OpenAI generated images with diffusion conditioned on CLIP image embeddings, with a leap in quality and prompt fidelity.

imagen.title: Imagen
imagen.summary: Google showed that a large language encoder (T5) improves prompt fidelity more than a bigger image model.

laion5b.title: LAION-5B
laion5b.summary: The LAION community released 5.85 billion CLIP-filtered image–text pairs from the web, open for research.
laion5b.impact: Stable Diffusion's data and a copyright flashpoint.

diffusionTransformers.title: Diffusion transformers (DiT)
diffusionTransformers.summary: Peebles and Xie replaced the U-Net in diffusion models with a transformer whose quality scales steadily with compute.
diffusionTransformers.impact: The backbone of SD3, Sora and newer generators.

flamingo.title: Flamingo
flamingo.summary: DeepMind connected a vision encoder to a frozen LLM through cross-attention, trained on interleaved images and text, enabling few-shot use on many tasks.
flamingo.impact: A template for later vision-language models.

instantNgp.title: Instant neural graphics primitives
instantNgp.summary: Müller and colleagues (NVIDIA) used a multiresolution hash encoding to train NeRFs in seconds instead of hours.
instantNgp.impact: Made NeRF practical; hash grids are now everywhere.

yoloV7.title: YOLOv7
yoloV7.summary: Wang, Bochkovskiy and Liao refined architecture and training (a trainable bag of freebies), beating every real-time detector of the time.
yoloV7.impact: Raised the bar for real-time detection.

classifierFreeGuidance.title: Classifier-free guidance
classifierFreeGuidance.summary: Ho and Salimans trained one model with and without the prompt, then pushed samples away from the unconditional prediction so images follow the prompt more closely.
classifierFreeGuidance.impact: The guidance scale knob in every text-to-image model.

dreamBooth.title: DreamBooth
dreamBooth.summary: Ruiz and colleagues (Google) fine-tuned a diffusion model on 3–5 photos of a subject to generate it in new scenes.
dreamBooth.impact: Started personalised generation, which with LoRA grew a whole ecosystem.

dreamFusion.title: DreamFusion
dreamFusion.summary: Poole and colleagues (Google) optimised a NeRF so a 2D diffusion model judges every rendered view to match the prompt (score distillation).

flowMatching.title: Flow matching
flowMatching.summary: Lipman and colleagues (Meta) trained models to learn a velocity field carrying noise straight to data, simpler and more stable than diffusion.
flowMatching.impact: The basis of Stable Diffusion 3, FLUX and many video models.

blip2.title: BLIP-2
blip2.summary: Salesforce bridged a frozen image encoder and a frozen LLM with a small Q-Former, very cheap to train.
blip2.impact: A recipe many open VLMs inherited.

controlNet.title: ControlNet
controlNet.summary: Zhang and colleagues added spatial conditions (edges, pose, depth) to a trained diffusion model without damaging it.

sigLip.title: SigLIP
sigLip.summary: Zhai and colleagues replaced the softmax in CLIP-style training with a pairwise sigmoid loss, more efficient at small batch sizes.
sigLip.impact: The image encoder many open VLMs use.

multimodalAssistants.title: Language models that see
multimodalAssistants.summary: Large language models took images as an extra input, answering questions and reasoning about visual content.
multimodalAssistants.impact: From fixed labels to open conversation.

groundingDino.title: Grounding DINO
groundingDino.summary: Liu and colleagues combined the DINO detector with language to detect any object described in text.

segmentAnything.title: Segment Anything (SAM)
segmentAnything.summary: Meta released a promptable segmentation model together with a dataset of over a billion masks.

dinoV2.title: DINOv2
dinoV2.summary: Meta trained self-supervised on 142 million curated images, producing features that work off the shelf for classification, segmentation and depth.

rtDetr.title: RT-DETR
rtDetr.summary: A Baidu team introduced an end-to-end transformer detector that runs in real time: a hybrid encoder processes multi-scale features efficiently, still with no NMS step, and it beat contemporary YOLO models on COCO in both speed and accuracy.

llava.title: LLaVA
llava.summary: Liu and colleagues fine-tuned an open LLM on image conversations generated by GPT-4, creating an open visual assistant.
llava.impact: Started the wave of open VLMs.

sdxl.title: SDXL
sdxl.summary: Stability AI released a larger open diffusion model with two text encoders and a refiner, at 1024 px.
sdxl.impact: For a time the most fine-tuned open generator.

gaussianSplatting.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting
gaussianSplatting.summary: Represents a scene as millions of Gaussian primitives, rendering in real time at quality comparable to NeRF.

dust3r.title: DUSt3R
dust3r.summary: Wang and colleagues predicted 3D point maps directly from a pair of images, with no camera parameters needed.

instructPix2Pix.title: InstructPix2Pix
instructPix2Pix.summary: Brooks, Holynski and Efros (Berkeley) taught a diffusion model to edit images from instructions such as "make it sunset", with training data made by GPT-3 and Stable Diffusion.

zero123.title: Zero-1-to-3
zero123.summary: Liu and colleagues (Columbia) fine-tuned Stable Diffusion to render an object from a new viewpoint given one image.
zero123.impact: Single image to 3D, the basis of image-to-3D models.

consistencyModels.title: Consistency models
consistencyModels.summary: Song and colleagues (OpenAI) trained models to jump from any point on the noise trajectory straight to a clean image, sampling in one or a few steps.
consistencyModels.impact: Opened the way to real-time generation instead of dozens of steps.

coTracker.title: CoTracker
coTracker.summary: Karaev and colleagues (Meta, Oxford) tracked thousands of points jointly through video with a Transformer, points helping each other through occlusion.
coTracker.impact: Long-range point tracking for robotics and video editing.

depthAnything.title: Depth Anything
depthAnything.summary: Yang and colleagues trained monocular depth on tens of millions of unlabelled images pseudo-labelled by a teacher.

yoloWorld.title: YOLO-World
yoloWorld.summary: Cheng and colleagues brought open-vocabulary detection into the YOLO architecture, in real time with text prompts.

stableDiffusion3.title: Stable Diffusion 3 and rectified flow
stableDiffusion3.summary: Esser and colleagues combined rectified flow with a multimodal transformer (MMDiT), clearly improving text rendering and prompt fidelity.

videoGeneration.title: Video generation
videoGeneration.summary: Diffusion models extended into the time dimension, producing short videos with coherent motion.
videoGeneration.impact: New challenge: temporal consistency and physics.

yoloV10.title: YOLOv10
yoloV10.summary: Wang and colleagues trained YOLO with dual label assignments to remove NMS, moving towards end-to-end real-time detection.

segmentAnything2.title: SAM 2
segmentAnything2.summary: Meta extended Segment Anything to video with a streaming memory, segmenting and tracking objects across frames.
segmentAnything2.impact: One model for image and video segmentation.

sora.title: Sora
sora.summary: OpenAI presented a diffusion Transformer over space-time patches that generates up to a minute of video from text.
sora.impact: Brought high-quality video generation and the "world simulator" idea to the public.

florence2.title: Florence-2
florence2.summary: Microsoft trained a small model (under a billion parameters) that does captioning, detection, grounding, segmentation and OCR just by changing the prompt.
florence2.impact: One compact model replacing many specialists.

var.title: Visual autoregressive modelling (VAR)
var.summary: Tian and colleagues generated images by next-scale prediction, from a 1×1 token map up to full resolution rather than token by token; NeurIPS 2024 best paper.
var.impact: Autoregressive models beat diffusion on ImageNet and follow LLM-style scaling laws.

mast3r.title: MASt3R
mast3r.summary: Leroy, Cabon and Revaud (Naver Labs) added matching descriptors to DUSt3R, pairing 3D points across images even under extreme viewpoint changes.
mast3r.impact: Matching and reconstruction in one model, replacing hand-crafted keypoints.

depthAnythingV2.title: Depth Anything V2
depthAnythingV2.summary: Yang and colleagues trained a teacher on synthetic images with precise depth, then pseudo-labelled tens of millions of real images to train students.
depthAnythingV2.impact: Sharp, robust single-image depth, widely used to condition generation.

vggt.title: VGGT
vggt.summary: Wang and colleagues (Oxford, Meta) predicted cameras, depth, point maps and point tracks from one to hundreds of images in a single forward pass; CVPR 2025 best paper.

dinoV3.title: DINOv3
dinoV3.summary: Meta scaled self-supervised learning to a 7-billion-parameter model and 1.7 billion images, giving high-quality dense features, satellite imagery included.

openVisionLanguage.title: Open vision–language models and embodied vision
openVisionLanguage.summary: Many open-weight vision–language models were released that run on personal machines and edge devices, while vision for robots and agents became a main research direction.
openVisionLanguage.impact: History still being written; suggest a milestone.

segmentAnything3.title: SAM 3
segmentAnything3.summary: Meta segmented and tracked every instance matching a concept given as text or an example image, instead of a single click.
segmentAnything3.impact: From "this object" to "every object of this kind".

sigLip2.title: SigLIP 2
sigLip2.summary: Google combined the sigmoid loss with captioning, self-distillation and masked prediction, giving a multilingual vision encoder better at both understanding and localisation.
sigLip2.impact: The default vision encoder for many open vision-language models.

cosmos.title: NVIDIA Cosmos
cosmos.summary: NVIDIA released open world foundation models trained on millions of hours of video to simulate the physical world for robots and self-driving.
cosmos.impact: Video generation as a simulator for training physical AI.

pixelScan.name: Digitising an image
pixelScan.caption: A scan line sweeps the photo and every grid cell is stored as a brightness value: the picture becomes a matrix of numbers.

perceptron.name: A perceptron learns a boundary
perceptron.caption: The neuron adds up weighted inputs; every mistake nudges the weights, so the line turns until it separates the two classes.

orientationCell.name: Orientation-selective cells
orientationCell.caption: A bar of light turns inside the receptive field; the neuron fires a burst of spikes only near its preferred orientation.

houghVoting.name: Hough voting
houghVoting.caption: Each point votes for every line through it (a curve in parameter space); where the curves cross is the line in the image.

wireframe.name: From edges to a 3D block
wireframe.caption: The image is read as edges and junctions; from that structure the machine infers a solid it can turn and view from any side.

fourier.name: Frequency analysis
fourier.caption: A signal is a sum of sine waves; the more frequencies you add, the closer the fit. Keeping only the strongest ones is how JPEG compresses.

shading.name: Shape from shading
shading.caption: As the light moves, brightness follows the direction each surface faces; inverting that gives the normals and the 3D shape.

histogramThreshold.name: Thresholding from the histogram
histogramThreshold.caption: The threshold slides along the histogram to the valley between the two peaks, the best split of foreground and background, then the image is binarised.

edgeDetect.name: Edge detection
edgeDetect.caption: A gradient filter sweeps the image and keeps only where brightness changes sharply: the outlines of objects.

scaleSpace.name: Scale space
scaleSpace.caption: The image is blurred more and more; each blob is detected at the scale that matches its size.

opticalFlow.name: Optical flow
opticalFlow.caption: Between two frames, every pixel gets a vector saying which way and how fast it moved.

ransac.name: RANSAC
ransac.caption: Pick two random points, fit a line, count who agrees; repeat a few times and keep the hypothesis with the most inliers, ignoring outliers.

twoView.name: Two-view geometry
twoView.caption: Two cameras see the same point; tracing both rays back through the image planes, they meet at its 3D position.

calibration.name: Camera calibration
calibration.caption: Photograph a checkerboard from several angles and detect its corners; since its true shape is known, the lens focal length and distortion can be solved.

snake.name: Active contour
snake.caption: A flexible curve is pulled towards image edges while staying smooth, shrinking until it hugs the object's boundary.

keypoints.name: Keypoints and matching
keypoints.caption: Find distinctive points that survive rotation and scale in both images, describe them, and link the pairs that match.

lbp.name: Local Binary Patterns
lbp.caption: Compare the 8 neighbours with the centre pixel, one bit each; the bits form a texture code, counted into a histogram.

bagOfWords.name: Bag of visual words
bagOfWords.caption: Each local patch is assigned to its nearest "word" in a codebook; the image becomes a histogram of word counts.

svmMargin.name: Maximum margin
svmMargin.caption: An SVM places the boundary so the gap to the nearest point of each class is as wide as possible; only a few support vectors decide it.

bilateral.name: Bilateral filter
bilateral.caption: Smooth by averaging neighbours, but only those with similar brightness, so noise disappears while edges stay sharp.

particles.name: Particle filter
particles.caption: The tracker keeps a cloud of guesses; each frame they are predicted, scored against the image, and resampled towards the likeliest spot.

textureGrow.name: Texture synthesis
textureGrow.caption: New texture grows one pixel at a time by finding the best-matching neighbourhood in the sample and copying the next pixel.

graphCut.name: Graph cut
graphCut.caption: Each pixel is a node and similar neighbours are strongly linked; the cheapest cut through the weak links separates object from background.

eigenfaces.name: Eigenfaces
eigenfaces.caption: Every face is the average face plus a few weighted eigenfaces; recognition just compares those weights.

slidingWindow.name: Sliding window
slidingWindow.caption: A fixed window slides across the image; at every position a classifier (Haar, HOG, part model) decides whether the object is there.

meanShift.name: Mean shift
meanShift.caption: Every point climbs towards the densest spot around it; points that stop at the same peak form one cluster.

seamlessBlend.name: Poisson blending
seamlessBlend.caption: The object is pasted by its gradients rather than its colours, so the seam vanishes and the colours blend into the new background.

ssimCompare.name: SSIM
ssimCompare.caption: Two images are compared window by window on brightness, contrast and structure, giving a similarity map close to human perception.

convolution.name: Convolution
convolution.caption: A small kernel slides over the image; each position gives one value of a feature map. Stack many layers and the network goes from edges to shapes to a label.

backprop.name: Backpropagation
backprop.caption: Signals flow forward to the output; the error flows back through every layer and adjusts each weight that caused it.

autoencoder.name: Autoencoder
autoencoder.caption: The image is squeezed through a narrow latent code and rebuilt; to manage that, the network must learn the features that matter most.

datasetGrid.name: Labelled datasets
datasetGrid.caption: Thousands to billions of images are collected and labelled; shared data and benchmarks are what push models forward.

multiView.name: Structure from motion
multiView.caption: Many photos from many angles are combined: each camera casts rays to shared points, building up a 3D point cloud and the camera poses.

pose.name: Pose estimation
pose.caption: The body is represented by keypoints at the joints and the limbs between them, estimated again in every frame, even for several people.

regionProposals.name: Two-stage detection
regionProposals.caption: First propose many regions that might hold an object, then classify each region and refine its bounding box.

gridDetection.name: One-stage detection
gridDetection.caption: A single look: the image is divided into a grid, and the cell holding an object's centre predicts its box and class directly, fast enough for real time.

faceEmbedding.name: Face embeddings
faceEmbedding.caption: Each face is mapped to a point; training pulls photos of the same person together and pushes different people apart.

inception.name: Inception module
inception.caption: Kernels of several sizes look at the same input in parallel; their outputs are concatenated so the network picks the right scale itself.

superResolution.name: Super-resolution
superResolution.caption: A network learns to fill in the detail a low-resolution image lost, turning blocky pixels into a sharp picture.

batchNorm.name: Batch normalization
batchNorm.caption: Activations that drift between layers are re-centred and re-scaled every batch, making training faster and more stable.

unet.name: U-Net
unet.caption: The encoder shrinks the image to grasp context and the decoder grows it back; skip connections carry detail across so the mask stays sharp.

styleTransfer.name: Style transfer
styleTransfer.caption: Content comes from one image, texture and colour from a painting; the output is optimised to match both.

residual.name: Residual connections
residual.caption: Each block only learns a correction added on top of a shortcut, so signals and gradients pass through hundreds of layers.

tracking.name: Multi-object tracking
tracking.caption: Objects are detected in every frame and linked to existing tracks, keeping their box and ID as they move.

imageTranslation.name: Image-to-image translation
imageTranslation.caption: A network learns to turn one kind of image into another (a sketch into a photo) and, with CycleGAN, back again to check consistency.

pyramid.name: Feature pyramid
pyramid.caption: Feature maps at several scales are linked top-down: small objects are caught at high resolution, large ones at low resolution.

instanceMask.name: Instance and panoptic segmentation
instanceMask.caption: Each object gets a box and then its own mask; panoptic segmentation also labels background stuff like road and sky.

spatioTemporal.name: 3D convolution
spatioTemporal.caption: The kernel slides through space and time across a stack of frames, so motion itself becomes a feature for recognising actions.

pixelMask.name: Semantic segmentation
pixelMask.caption: Every pixel gets a class: first coarse blocks, then refined to the true outline of each object.

gan.name: GAN
gan.caption: A generator forges images from noise while a discriminator learns to spot fakes; the contest makes the fakes ever more realistic.

patchAttention.name: Self-attention over patches
patchAttention.caption: The image is cut into patches used as tokens; each patch looks at every other one and decides how much attention each deserves.

contrastive.name: Self-supervised contrastive learning
contrastive.caption: Two augmented views of the same image are pulled together in embedding space and other images pushed away, with no labels.

nerfRays.name: NeRF
nerfRays.caption: From the camera, each ray passes through a learned volume; accumulating colour and density along it gives one pixel's colour.

setPrediction.name: Set prediction with object queries
setPrediction.caption: A fixed set of object queries each claims exactly one object or says "nothing here"; no anchors or NMS needed.

diffusion.name: Diffusion
diffusion.caption: Starting from pure noise, the model removes noise over many steps, steered by the prompt, until the image appears.

imageTokens.name: Image generation as tokens
imageTokens.caption: Text and image are both token sequences; the model writes the image out one token at a time after the text that describes it.

imageTextMatch.name: Image–text contrastive learning
imageTextMatch.caption: Images and captions are embedded in one space; true pairs light up the diagonal while wrong pairs fade, which enables zero-shot classification.

shiftedWindows.name: Shifted windows
shiftedWindows.caption: Attention is computed only within small windows to save compute; the next layer shifts the windows by half so information crosses their borders.

maskedPatches.name: Masked image modelling
maskedPatches.caption: About 75% of the patches are hidden and the model must paint them back; to do so it has to understand the image.

visualChat.name: Vision-language model
visualChat.caption: The image is encoded into tokens fed to an LLM; the user asks in words and the model looks at the relevant region and answers.

controlNet.name: Conditional control
controlNet.caption: A sketch, pose or edge map steers the denoising, so the generated image follows that structure.

textGrounding.name: Open-vocabulary detection
textGrounding.caption: Each phrase in the prompt is linked to its box in the image, even for classes never seen in training.

promptMask.name: Promptable segmentation
promptMask.caption: One click (or box) is enough: the model returns the mask of whatever lies under it, for any kind of object.

splatting.name: Gaussian splatting
splatting.caption: A cloud of soft coloured Gaussians is moved and reshaped until it renders the scene, fast enough to view in real time.

depthMap.name: Monocular depth
depthMap.caption: From a single photo the model estimates how far away every pixel is: near is bright, far is dark.

videoFrames.name: Video generation
videoFrames.caption: Frames are denoised together rather than one by one, so the motion between them stays consistent over time.

videoMask.name: Video segmentation with memory
videoMask.caption: Click the object in the first frame; a memory stores its features and carries the mask through every following frame.

conceptMask.name: Concept segmentation
conceptMask.caption: A short noun phrase such as "tree" finds and masks every instance of that concept, not just one.

kalman.name: Predict and correct
kalman.caption: Each step the filter predicts the next position and its uncertainty grows; a measurement then pulls the estimate towards it and the uncertainty shrinks.

kMeansClusters.name: k-means clustering
kMeansClusters.caption: Every point takes the colour of its nearest centre, then each centre moves to the mean of its points; a few rounds and the clusters settle.

stereoDisparity.name: Stereo disparity
stereoDisparity.caption: The same object appears shifted between the left and right images; the nearer it is, the larger the shift, so the disparity map is a depth map.

isoSurface.name: Extracting a surface from a grid
isoSurface.caption: Each grid cell checks whether its corners lie inside or outside the shape; joining the crossings on its edges traces the boundary (in 3D, a triangle mesh).

pointAlign.name: Aligning point clouds
pointAlign.caption: Each point is linked to its nearest neighbour in the other cloud; the best rotation and translation is applied, and this repeats until the clouds line up.

seamCarve.name: Seam carving
seamCarve.caption: Find the top-to-bottom seam through the least detailed pixels and remove it; the image gets narrower while the main objects stay undistorted.

pointCloud.name: Learning on point clouds
pointCloud.caption: The same small network turns every point into a feature vector; max-pooling merges them into an order-independent descriptor used to classify the object.

saliencyHeatmap.name: Explanation heatmap
saliencyHeatmap.caption: The gradient of the predicted class shows which feature-map regions mattered; overlaid on the image, it lights up where the model looked.

nextScale.name: Next-scale prediction
nextScale.caption: The model predicts a 1×1 token map, then 2×2, 4×4 and 8×8, each conditioned on the coarser ones, so the image sharpens from layout to detail.

flowPaths.name: Paths from noise to data
flowPaths.caption: Each noise sample follows a learned velocity field to a real image; the straighter the paths, the fewer steps needed, down to a single jump.

backgroundModel.name: Background modelling
backgroundModel.caption: Every pixel remembers its usual background colour; pixels that differ from that model are marked as moving foreground.

dropoutNet.name: Dropout
dropoutNet.caption: At every training step a random set of neurons is switched off, so the network learns redundant paths instead of relying on a few units.

channelAttention.name: Channel attention
channelAttention.caption: Each channel is squeezed to one number; a small network uses those numbers to boost useful channels and damp the rest.
